0.description: High direct flight density routes between neighboring economic hubs, driven by low-cost carriers with rapid departure day price spikes.

1.description: High-ticket intercontinental corridors with premium cabin reliance, wide fare dispersion, and significant advance booking lead times.

2.description: Major domestic cross-country connecting lines connecting primary Indian metros, characterized by mixed direct/connecting traffic.

3.description: High-volume short-haul international business and transit hubs with elevated baseline yields and steady business traveler demand.

ethical_considerations.title: Consumer Empowerment vs. Information Asymmetry
ethical_considerations.description: Airlines utilize sophisticated revenue management algorithms to exploit consumer willingness-to-pay. This segmentation model levels the playing field by providing transparent 'Book Now vs. Wait' intelligence to prevent consumers from overpaying.

ethical_considerations.title: Price Gouging in Inelastic Emergency Corridors
ethical_considerations.description: Clusters identified with extreme last-minute surge ratios (e.g. Cluster 2) often represent inelastic, non-discretionary routes (medical emergencies, urgent family travel). Ethical airline pricing frameworks should advocate for caps on surge gouging on captive corridors.

ethical_considerations.title: Algorithmic Collusion Prevention
ethical_considerations.description: Care must be taken so that pricing intelligence tools are not inverted by airline carriers to coordinate tacit price collusion across segmented route archetypes.

ethical_considerations.title: Responsible Use for Travel Aggregators
ethical_considerations.description: Recommendations must clearly display statistical confidence scores and sample sizes (as done on FarePredictor) rather than absolute guarantees, acknowledging inherent stochastic volatility in airline revenue management.

limitations.title: Observation Horizon Truncation (50-Day Limit)
limitations.description: The dataset observes fares up to 49 days prior to departure. It does not capture ultra-early bird inventory released 6 to 12 months ahead, potentially truncating the earliest phases of airline yield curves.

limitations.title: Survivorship Bias (Inventory Censoring)
limitations.description: Scraped fare datasets only observe available, unbooked seats. Flights that sell out early disappear from the scrape, artificially biasing late-stage fare observations toward either high unsold premium inventory or distressed low-demand seats.

limitations.title: Geographical & Hub Bias
limitations.description: The Kaggle dataset focuses predominantly on primary Indian metropolitan hubs (Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Chennai). Route dynamics for regional tier-2/tier-3 underserved routes may exhibit different elasticity and monopoly patterns.

limitations.title: Exogenous Factor Omission
limitations.description: Macroeconomic variables such as jet fuel (ATF) fluctuations, seasonality (monsoon vs holiday wedding seasons), baggage ancillary fees, and sudden airline operational disruptions are not explicitly modeled in ticket prices.
